articles.title: Ukraine: Zelenskyy and Hungary's Magyar meet amid thaw in ties
articles.summary: Hungary's Prime Minister Peter Magyar has arrived in Ukraine for meetings with President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and ethnic Hungarians. Both leaders say they want better relations after a change of…

image.caption: The tone between Budapest and Kyiv changed considerably after Hungarians elected Peter Magyar (right) to replace long-serving pro-Russian PM Viktor Orban [FILE: October 2026]Image: Stephanie Lecocq/REUTERS

blocks.text: Hungary's new Prime Minister Peter Magyar arrived in Ukraine on Tuesday afternoon for meetings with President Volodymyr Zelenskyy as well as with ethnic Hungarians living in the west of the country.

The meeting comes as both say they want better relations after a change of leadership in Budapest — no doubt a welcome change for Kyiv after years of Viktor Orban obstructing funding for its self-defense against full-scaler Russian invasion.

Ukraine's Zelenskyy posted his thanks for the meeting with a photo on X, writing: "A visit that is sure to bring positive results. We already have agreements in the areas of politics, energy, and infrastructure. Thank you!"
Despite his softer approach, Magyar has said Hungary will not be sending arms to Kyiv while at the same time vowing, "we stand with Ukraine against the Russian aggressor."
Rights of ethnic Hungarians tied to war support and EU accession talks

Magyar has insisted that the rights of tens of thousands of ethnic Hungarians in the Transcarpathia — a region that was part of Austria-Hungary until the end of World War I and situated at the borders of Ukraine, Hungary, Poland, Romania and Slovakia — be resolved before Budapest can wholeheartedly back Ukraine and its possible accession to the European Union.

Relations deteriorated significantly over the issue in 2017, when Kyiv passed a law making Ukrainian the official language of all secondary education in Ukraine, something Budapest viewed as discriminatory toward ethnic Hungarians.

Last month, Ukrainian lawmakers passed legislation allowing ethnic minorities in the country expanded rights regarding the teaching and use of their native languages. The move was welcomed by Budapest and Hungary dropped its opposition to Brussels opening accession talks with Ukraine.
Magyar pitched this week's trip — the first to Transcarpathia by a Hungarian prime minister since 2015 — in April, after defeating Orban.

Before departing for Ukraine, the Hungarian leader said: "I hope these talks will be successful. I think this is a historic day and a good opportunity to put Ukrainian-Hungarian relations on a new footing and to rebuild trust as we did with our other neighbors."

articles.title: NPC: 11 gov't agencies yet to fully explain data breaches
articles.summary: The National Privacy Commission (NPC) said that 11 government agencies have yet to submit a full breach report following hacking incidents.

blocks.text: Published November 25, 2026 12:24am
The National Privacy Commission (NPC) said that 11 government agencies have yet to submit a full breach report following hacking incidents.
NPC spokesperson Jose Amelito Belarmino II said that a total of 13 government agencies were reportedly hacked.

“Inaantay namin iyong full breach report ng ilang ahensiya. In fact, doon sa 13 na government agencies na na-breach at nag-report sa amin noong between November 9 to November 13, dalawa pa lamang iyong nagsusumite ng full breach report. So iyong iba po, wala pa pong isinusumite,” Belarmino said on the Bagong Pilipinas Ngayon public briefing on Tuesday,

(We are waiting for the full breach report from several agencies. In fact, from the 13 government agencies that were breached from November 9 to 13, only two submitted their full breach report. The others have not submitted.)
The Philippine Amusement and Gaming Corporation (PAGCOR) and the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) were the two that reportedly already submitted, but Belarmino did not name the other 11.
In addition to the 13 agencies, the Department of Migrant Workers was also hacked. It must also submit a report.
Belarmino said that under the law, agencies that were hacked are required to submit a full report five days after they notify the NPC.
Failure to submit the full breach report was already a violation, said Belarmino. —LDF, GMA News

Since last week, tradespeople who completed an apprenticeship and earned their certification in a Red Seal trade on or after April 1, 2025, have been able to apply for a $5,000 completion bonus.

articles.title: Monday Night Football power outage leaves fans and players in the dark
articles.summary: The lights at Northwest Stadium went out during the third quarter of Monday night’s game between the Cincinnati Bengals and the Washington Commanders, leading to a delay of about four minutes.

image.caption: Players look on after the lights go out during the third quarter of the game between the Cincinnati Bengals and Washington Commanders at Northwest Stadium in Landover, Md., Monday. (Amber Searls/Imagn Images/Reuters)

blocks.text: World·New
The lights at Northwest Stadium went out during the third quarter of Monday night’s game between the Cincinnati Bengals and the Washington Commanders, leading to a delay of about four minutes.
Lights went out during third quarter of Cincinnati-Washington game
Who turned out the lights?

Fans and players were left in the dark Monday when the lights went out at Northwest Stadium during the third quarter of the game between the Cincinnati Bengals and the Washington Commanders, leading to a delay of about four minutes and widespread, albeit temporary, confusion.

The Commanders were in the red zone, trailing 10-7, when the stadium in Landover, Md., went dark. A collective shout emerged from the crowd, referees blew their whistles, and play-by-play announcer Joe Buck observed, "Somebody turned out the lights."
"Somebody leaned against the wall," he joked a moment later.
"We'll see how long this takes to get them back up and running," quipped analyst Troy Aikman, as the two did their best to fill airspace before going to commercial.
The lights in the stadium went out at the beginning of the third quarter of Bengals-Commanders. https://t.co/f3yeTJONCt—espn
The lights returned after a brief official timeout. The crowd roared and Buck exclaimed: "Let there be light!"
The game resumed and in the end, the Commanders won 22-20.
Later in the broadcast, Buck offered up an explanation for the brief outage.
"The official word is that the lighting vendor never disabled the regularly scheduled maintenance for 10 p.m.," he said.
"It’s a weekday thing, and they forgot it was a Monday night game."
Aikman chuckled in response.
Fans had their say online — some calling it unacceptable, and many joking that the lighting vendor was going to be fired.
"Somebody's getting a very awkward phone call from Roger Goodell tomorrow morning," one fan wrote on X, referring to the NFL commissioner.
The lights at Northwest Stadium went out early in the third quarter, interrupting play. (Julia Demaree Nikhinson/The Associated Press)

The Bengals faced another power outage earlier this month during a game in Madrid, which interrupted the game with fewer than two minutes left of play. Neither outage compares to the 2013 Super Bowl blackout that plunged the stadium into darkness for 34 minutes.

Perhaps the most memorable pro sports lights gaffe was in 1988, when a power outage at Boston Garden halted a tie game between the Boston Bruins and Edmonton Oilers in the NHL Stanley Cup final. The game could not resume and fans were sent home.

items: The power outage that ended a tie game in the 1988 Stanley Cup final
Super Bowl blackout caused by faulty device

blocks.text: Two years later, the same two teams would meet again in the 1990 Stanley Cup final and the power went out again during a tie game, once again at Boston Garden.
That time, however, the lights were restored and the Oilers won 3-2 in triple overtime.
The 1988 power outage at Boston Garden

articles.title: Ukraine's bid for NATO membership and more air defense remain controversial
articles.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy is calling for the rapid acceptance of his country into NATO. However, the necessary unanimity for this is lacking, as shown during the NATO Parliamentary…

image.caption: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy participated in the NATO Parliamentary Assembly in Berlin via video conferenceImage: Liesa Johannssen/REUTERS

blocks.text: It took a while for the video call to connect. When Volodymyr Zelenskyy finally greeted the delegates in Berlin, applause broke out. The Ukrainian president appealed to the gathered parliamentarians from 32 NATO member states to keep supporting his country, especially against the massive aerial bombardment from Russia.

"Dear friends, winter is now ahead of us. And of course, our number one priority is air defense," Zelenskyy told the delegates. His country urgently needs more Patriot and other comprehensive anti-air attack systems. "And your countries have them. Missiles that can stop Russian ballistic missiles should not be sitting in warehouses collecting dust. And we say this openly. Please help us with this."
Western allies boost Ukraine's defenses but clash over deep strikes
Ukraine seeks to join NATO

Zelenskyy renewed his call for his country to join the NATO military alliance. That issue is not for the NATO Parliamentary Assembly, which was gathered for its 72nd annual meeting in Berlin, to decide. But it was important to the Ukrainian president to reiterate his request.

After the war ends, Ukraine needs strong security guarantees and NATO could ensure those. "Wouldn't it be more effective to simply bring Ukraine into NATO?" Zelenskyy asked, arguing: "Wouldn't that be better for all of us, for everyone? Cheaper to put in place? And more reliable when it comes to actually protecting security?"

There is conflict among NATO members about the possibility of admitting Ukraine. The alliance has affirmed multiple times that the path to membership stands open to Ukraine — however, in the long term rather than the near future. This is primarily because of the ongoing war and the possible assistance obligations of other NATO countries for Ukraine, which was attacked by Russia.

NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte rejected the Ukrainian demands at the summit, which for the first time in 26 years was held in Berlin. Ukraine had entry prospects; however, NATO members currently lack unanimity on this issue. NATO alone decides who becomes a member. "There is total clarity on that within the alliance," Rutte said.
If Russia attacked NATO, would Germany be prepared?
Merz: Denying Ukraine NATO membership in 2008 'was a mistake'

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz advocated for Ukraine to receive security guarantees similar to what NATO members have, in the instance of a possible ceasefire. In retrospect, it was clear "what a mistake it was not to follow the American suggestion back in 2008 at the NATO summit in Bucharest to admit Ukraine as a member," Merz said at a joint press conference following a meeting with Rutte.

Whether or not a NATO entry for Ukraine could be part of negotiations with Russia is another question, according to Rutte. He approved of current US efforts to bring about peace talks, and how Europe was closely consulting with Ukraine and the US for a unified position. "But it is also to test now whether Putin is willing to play ball, and then these issues might come up again."

The Russian invasion of Ukraine has led to NATO arming itself on a massive scale. Members have committed to raising their countries' defense spending to 5% of their gross domestic product (GDP) by 2035.

Rutte warned that all the allies needed a credible path to get there, "and ideally, they get there sooner than 2035." In addition, he said weapons production among member states needed to further increase because "right now, demand still far exceeds the supply."
Why Germany's military ambitions face a battle at home
Germany's military budget has had a massive increase

The contribution by Germany's Bundeswehr armed forces to NATO was explained by Carsten Breuer, Germany's highest-ranking soldier. For example, the massive increase in military spending: "Our defense budget has tripled since 2021. The goal is to achieve the 5% target, which was set at the summit in The Hague, well before 2035." In the coming year, Germany's defense budget has risen to more than €139 billion ($151 billion).

The Bundeswehr was further developing into a "constantly modernized, effective and innovative army, Breuer said. Also, a much larger one than before: "To reach our current capability goals we are expanding the Bundeswehr to a total of 460,000 soldiers by the mid-2030s," the German chief of defense said. Of those, 200,000 are to be reservists. "This is like walking a tightrope because we must find the right balance between growth and operational readiness."

Following his speech, Breuer answered questions from the delegates who showed keen interest in the developments. The discussion was a preview of Breuer's new post: He has been voted in as the new chair of the NATO Military Committee and will move to the alliance's headquarters in Brussels mid-next year. Then he will become the principal military advisor to NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte. "I take this election as a sign of recognition that Germany has now accepted its responsibility as well as its role in security policy," Breuer commented.
This article was originally written in German.

articles.title: Irish plan offers Burnham breakthrough on Made in Europe
articles.summary: Irish presidency of EU proposes giving UK ‘partner’ status on assembly of cars in possible boost to reset of relations

blocks.text: The UK wwould not have to follow the EU and apply tariffs on Chinese car imports under an Irish proposal that could prove another breakthrough for the prime minister, Andy Burnham, in his reset of relations with the bloc.

Ireland, which holds the rotating EU presidency and plays a central role in steering legislation, has come up with a compromise under which the UK would be included in the bloc’s new “Made in Europe” legislation without having to align with the EU’s trade policies.

Made in Europe, or the Industrial Accelerator Act (IAA), is designed to protect the bloc’s supply chains from cheap competition, mainly from China, particularly in the automotive and clean energy sectors.

It is understood that in a fourth compromise text, due to be considered by EU competition ministers on 3 December, Ireland has proposed giving the European Economic Area, Switzerland and the UK “partner” status for the assembly of cars.
This would allow not only cars such as the Mini, made at BMW’s Oxford factory, to qualify as European, but also vehicles made by the Japanese firm Nissan at its vast Sunderland plant.
Under the compromise, a “partner” country would agree to mutual access to any subsidies available to EU-owned assembly plants, and to public procurement contracts for fleet cars.

Irish negotiators have also suggested giving Japan and South Korea, which lobbied hard against the original Made in Europe proposals, access to public procurement and other public support schemes for car parts and components.

A spokesperson for the Irish presidency said: “Having listened closely to all member states, the presidency has proposed a pragmatic and balanced way forward on the IAA to deliver for European competitiveness.”
Burnham last week took the biggest step towards deeper ties with the EU since Brexit, sealing deals to ease trade and create a mobility scheme for young people.
The latest iteration of the IAA text is designed to reflect the car sector’s position as a cornerstone of European industry.

France, which championed the legislation, originally opposed the inclusion of the UK at all but dropped its opposition last month on condition that the UK dynamically align with the EU on tariffs on Chinese vehicles.

But this caused further tensions with the UK. The business secretary, Jonathan Reynolds, insisted the British government would not be coerced into imposing tariffs on Chinese vehicles and would only take steps that were in the national interest.

Mike Hawes, the chief executive of the Society of Motor Manufacturers and Traders, said the UK “should not become collateral damage” from measures intended to address concerns arising elsewhere in the global market.
The UK car industry has argued that it is so intertwined with its EU counterparts that both sides would be damaged if the UK was not included in Made in Europe.
after newsletter promotion
Hawes said: “It is essential that the final arrangements recognise the unique UK-EU automotive relationship as allies in adversity, and do not create new barriers to our shared supply chains.”
The latest proposal will be discussed by an EU working group involving industry leaders and EU member states on Friday, before being finessed further for consideration by ministers.

European carmakers are attempting to respond to a flood of cheap Chinese electric vehicles into the bloc. ⁠Volkswagen began wage talks ⁠with labour representatives on ​Tuesday amid mounting worker anger over deep cost cuts, with protesters carrying black coffins to symbolise what they said was the death of trust and the company’s future prospects.

blocks.caption: Coffins at a Volkswagen protest in Emden, Germany, on Tuesday. Photograph: Leon Kuegeler/Reuters

blocks.text: China faces further restrictions on its trade with EU: tariffs were imposed on Chinese EV imports in 2024, and quotas agreed with Beijing in October come into force on 1 December.

The Chinese electric vehicle maker BYD ⁠said on ⁠Tuesday that it had entered into exclusive ⁠negotiations with the billionaire Jim Ratcliffe’s Ineos Automotive to buy ⁠its manufacturing plant in ‌Hambach, France, ‌as it seeks ‌more European production ahead of Made in Europe legislation expected next year.
Separately, Ineos said on Tuesday it would begin production of its Grenadier 4x4 in the US in 2028.

articles.title: HIV infections could rise amid aid cuts, UN warns
articles.summary: The impact of United States government funding cuts has been dramatic for many HIV programs, UNAIDS warned. The agency expects that 2027 data to show an increase in new infections after being on the…

image.caption: US contributions for HIV programs have dropped by 26% between 2024 and 2025 [FILE: February 2025]Image: MANDEL NGAN/AFP via Getty Images

blocks.text: New HIV infections could rise next year for the first time in years, reversing a historic decline amid funding cuts and anti-rights campaigns, the United Nations (UN) warned on Tuesday.

"The world has moved closer towards controlling the HIV pandemic, but changes in funding and resulting service disruptions jeopardize this progress," the UNAIDS agency said in its annual global update.

AIDS-related death numbers has fallen to its lowest in more than two decades. According to the organization, this was made possible by broader access to treatment and improvements in the quality of care programs.
The virus claimed roughly 570,000 lives globally in 2025. This means almost 1,600 people died everyday. In comparison, this figure was 600,000 in 2024 and 1.3 million in 2010.
Based on data from 172 countries, the agency estimated that 41 million people worldwide were living with HIV in 2025, of whom 32.1 million were receiving antiretroviral treatment.

The wider use of antiretroviral medication also reduces the risk of HIV transmission, the organization said. It estimates that 1.2 million people contracted HIV in 2025, down from 1.3 million the year before. The peak in 1994 saw 3.5 million.

blocks.caption: UNAIDS said Lenacapavir, an injection administered just twice a year, has marked another turning point in HIV prevention [FILE: July 2024]Image: Nardus Engelbrecht/AP/picture alliance

blocks.text: "HIV, which was once a death sentence, has become a manageable health condition for millions of people thanks to life-saving HIV medicines," said UNAIDS.
'Dramatic impacts' of US aid cuts
Despite the encouraging data so far, cuts to international funding have hampered efforts to fight HIV, the agency warned.
HIV programs faced an 18-percent decrease in international financing over the past year, said UNAIDS.
"Funding losses have destabilized HIV programs worldwide, coinciding with a wider contraction in official development assistance over the years," it said.
Although the United States remains the largest international donor for HIV programs, its contributions dropped by 26% between 2024 and 2025.
How USAID cuts could result in higher HIV transmission
After dismantling USAID, the world's largest foreign aid agency, last year, the Donald Trump administration has sought to replace decades of aid with new bilateral deals.
"The impact of the United States government funding cuts has been especially dramatic given the reliance of many countries on its support for core HIV programs," said UNAIDS.
Meanwhile disbursements from the Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria dropped by 13% in 2025.
Next year's data may show rising infections

"We are on the cusp of ending AIDS – this has been the greatest story of global ​health – and just when we should finish it, cuts and the rolling back of human rights is ​threatening to take away our gains," Winnie Byanyima, executive director of UNAIDS, told ​Reuters.
"We haven't ‌got the data yet, but we see the signs. We see all the signs of reversals," she added.
Byanyima predicted that data released in 2027 would begin to reflect a rise in new HIV infections.
In 2015, the UN set a goal to end AIDS by 2030.

articles.title: 'Significant' wind, waves and rainfall forecast for coastal B.C.: Environment Canada
articles.summary: More rainy, windy weather is expected on Vancouver Island and along other parts of the B.C. coast, coinciding with a run of king tides, according to Environment Canada.

image.caption: Rainfall, wind and coastal flooding warnings are in effect for parts of Vancouver Island on Tuesday. (Claire Palmer/CBC)

blocks.text: British Columbia·New
More rainy, windy weather is expected on Vancouver Island and along other parts of the B.C. coast, coinciding with a run of king tides, according to Environment Canada.
Coastal flooding warnings are in effect for parts of Vancouver Island, the Central Coast and Haida Gwaii
More rainy, windy weather is expected on Vancouver Island and along other parts of the B.C. coast, coinciding with a run of king tides, according to Environment and Climate Change Canada.

The federal department has issued coastal flooding warnings for parts of the Central Coast, western Vancouver Island and Haida Gwaii. It says moderate storm surge and large waves will come alongside very high tides, known as king tides.
Together, they could elevate water levels 20 to 50 centimetres above the highest astronomical tides, Environment Canada says.
A coastal flooding statement is also in effect for parts of the South Coast, with water levels expected to rise and peak on Thursday.

items: What are king tides?

blocks.text: Rainfall amounts of up to 200 millimetres are expected on some parts of Vancouver Island, and some higher amounts are possible locally, according to Environment Canada.
"Rainfall rates will ease Wednesday morning but another potent storm arrives late Wednesday afternoon bringing a new round of significant precipitation and strong winds."
The department is warning landslides could occur in vulnerable areas such as steep slopes, deforested areas or recent burn scars.

items: More stories from Vancouver Island

blocks.text: Wind warnings are also in effect for parts of Vancouver Island and the Sunshine Coast.
Gusts could reach 110 km/h at times in certain areas. The winds are expected to ease later Tuesday morning.
Local utility outages are possible, according to Environment Canada, and residents are urged to secure loose objects.
The River Forecast Centre has issued a high streamflow advisory for Vancouver Island, as rivers are "expected to rise rapidly in response to rainfall."

The Tla-o-qui-aht First Nation on the west coast of Vancouver Island has issued an evacuation alert for some properties along the shoreline due to flooding. Anyone in the affected area must be ready to leave at a moment's notice.

articles.title: More than 300 Russians killed as Moscow props up Mali’s junta, leaked data reveals
articles.summary:
Records list 349 deaths in three years in Mali and also shed light on Russia’s military activity elsewhere in Africa

When the attack on Kidal began before dawn on 25 April this year, the…
articles.byline: Pjotr Sauer, Michael Goodier, Harriet Agerholm and Philip McMahon

blocks.text: When the attack on Kidal began before dawn on 25 April this year, the Russian fighters were caught off guard. Within the first hour, checkpoints on the outskirts of the remote desert city nestled among the rocky hills of northern Mali had fallen to the insurgents, who pushed towards the police station where fierce fighting erupted.

“Everything was happening at once. Explosions were going off all around us, people were shouting,” recalled a former member of Russia’s Africa Corps who was stationed in Mali at the time and spoke on condition of anonymity. “Nobody knew where the enemy was coming from.”

The Kremlin-controlled forces and their Malian allies were facing a coordinated surprise assault by the al-Qaida-linked JNIM and the Tuareg-led Azawad Liberation Front (FLA), whose fighters used suicide car bombs and drones to break through the city’s defences.

blocks.caption: The view from a helicopter flying over a convoy of tankers heading towards Mali’s capital, Bamako, in May 2026, posted on the X account of the Africa Corps. Photograph: Africa Corps/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: Leaked Russian state records suggest the losses were heavy that day. Death certificates of Russian fighters killed in Mali, held by Rosstat, Russia’s state statistics agency, were obtained by the hacker groups Cyber Partisans and Silent Crow and analysed by the Guardian.

The records show that 43 Russians died in Mali on 25 April, including six in Kidal and one in nearby Aguelhok. Others were recorded as dying in the capital, Bamako, and in Gao, where rebels shot down a Russian military helicopter that day.

By the following morning, the Russians had abandoned Kidal, which Russian mercenaries had helped capture in November 2023 and which Moscow had since held up as a showcase of its growing influence in Africa.
In all, the records list 349 Russian deaths in Mali between September 2023 and September 2026, most of which the Guardian was able to link to known battles with rebel groups.

blocks.caption: A billboard in Bamako carrying birthday wishes for Vladimir Putin, October 2024. Photograph: AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: The figures offer a previously unseen glimpse into the human cost of Moscow’s efforts to prop up Mali’s military junta, in what has become Russia’s largest military deployment in Africa.
Two western officials who have travelled to Mali and were shown the data said the death toll was higher than previously estimated.
“That’s over 10% of Russia’s forces killed in action,” said one of the officials, speaking on condition of anonymity because they were not authorised to comment publicly.
Moscow does not publish its losses in Africa, and its foreign ministry did not respond to a request for comment.

The Wagner private military group, led by the warlord Yevgeny Prigozhin, first arrived in Mali in late 2021, a year after a military coup had toppled President Ibrahim Boubacar Keïta. French forces were ordered to leave the country as relations with the junta deteriorated, bringing an end to France’s decade-long counter-terrorism operation and leaving Russia as the regime’s main foreign protector.

blocks.caption: Three Russian mercenaries operating in northern Mali, January 2022 Photograph: French army/AP

blocks.text: Wagner handed over its operations in Mali to the Africa Corps in June 2025, two years after Prigozhin led a failed mutiny on Moscow that discredited the group in the eyes of the Kremlin. By that summer, British intelligence estimated that about 2,000 Africa Corps personnel were deployed in the country.

The Africa Corps, closely overseen by Russian military intelligence, currently provides backing to several African governments in return for payment or lucrative contracts granting access to natural resources.

Despite the Russian presence, Mali’s security situation has continued to deteriorate. In late July 2024, Russian and Malian forces fought Tuareg separatists for several days near Tinzaouaten, on the Algerian border.
Wagner at the time issued a rare statement admitting losses, including the death of a commander, but gave no figure. Estimates from Russian sources ranged from about 20 to more than 80 dead.

blocks.caption: Graves of Wagner fighters in a cemetery near the village of Bakinskaya, in Russia’s Krasnodar region, January 2023. Photograph: Reuters

blocks.text: The Rosstat records list 70 Russians who died on 27 July 2024, all but one of them in the Kidal region. The figures make the battle of Tinzaouaten the deadliest single day for Russian forces in Africa since Wagner mercenaries first deployed to the continent in 2017.

The toll in Mali may have been driven up by Ukraine, which has extended its war against Russia to the Sahel. Kyiv has been assisting Tuareg rebels there, according to two people with knowledge of the operations. CNN has reported that about 15 Ukrainian specialists were deployed to Mali to help local rebel forces fighting Russian troops.

The records are probably an undercount. Registration often lags, and no Russian deaths in Mali are recorded for March 2026 although at least three Africa Corps fighters were reported killed in an ambush near Nampala that month.

The leaked data also sheds light on Russia’s military activity elsewhere in Africa. Central African Republic, where Wagner fighters guard the president, Faustin-Archange Touadéra, accounts for 30 deaths. While not all could be linked to known incidents, three men died on the night drones struck Wagner camps in Kaga-Bandoro in December 2023.

In Libya, where Russian forces back the eastern commander Khalifa Haftar and use his airbases as a supply route to their deployments in the Sahel, some of the recorded deaths were probably linked to a helicopter crash at the Maaten al-Sarra base in February 2026. On Sunday, Ukrainian drones sunk a Russian warship off the coast of Libya; it is unclear whether there were any casualties.

blocks.caption: Supporters of Niger’s ruling junta hold up a Russian flag in Niamey, August 2023.  Photograph: Sam Mednick/AP

blocks.text: In Niger, where Russia’s Africa Corps moved in after the military junta expelled French and US troops, a Russian fighter died two days after Islamic State militants attacked Niamey airport in January, a previously unreported casualty.

Moscow has in recent months stepped up its effort to show it is back in control in Mali. On 6 October, Malian troops and the Africa Corps recaptured Kidal after what the army called an air and ground campaign.

A report this month by the US-based Conflict Insights Group (CIG) found that the Africa Corps had sharply increased its use of drones in Mali, including Lancet suicide drones, amid an intensifying air campaign.

The group wrote that the drone campaign had also targeted civilians, boostering support for the rebels. “Civilian deaths in the intensified air campaign, which the Africa Corps leads, are likely to aid insurgent recruitment,” it said.

blocks.caption: Vladimir Putin and the Malian junta leader, Assimi Goita, at the Kremlin in June 2025. Photograph: Pavel Bednyakov/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: A western diplomat who works in the region said the attacks in late April had punctured the image of Russian military invincibility that Moscow and the junta had cultivated among Malians.
“Russia still wields considerable influence in Mali, but patience with its military performance is wearing thin.”

articles.title: Palace to Cayetano: Lead the way
articles.summary: Lead the way.

blocks.text: November 25, 2026 | 12:00am
Senate Minority Leader Alan Cayetano on February 9, 2026.
STAR / Ryan Baldemor
MANILA, Philippines — Lead the way.

This was Malacañang’s challenge to Senate Minority Leader Alan Cayetano, who urged the central bank and economic managers on Monday to come up with a way for generous Filipinos to voluntarily share in repaying the country’s debt.

“He (Cayetano) said it’s voluntary. So it is hard to craft a law if it becomes mandatory. But if there are kind-hearted persons who are willing to start it, it would be better if we see Sen. Alan Cayetano himself starting it,” Palace press officer Claire Castro said yesterday.
According to Castro, Cayetano could “serve as a model” by contributing money to reduce the Philippines’ debt.
Cayetano floated the idea during the Senate’s plenary debates on the proposed P7.2-trillion national budget for next year.
He noted that every Filipino owes more than P170,000 since the national government debt stood at P19.66 trillion as of the third quarter.
Despite the backlash, Cayetano stood firm on his proposal.
He pointed out that the lack of such a mechanism for volunteerism reflects a deeper “crisis of confidence” and distrust in public officials.

“There’s no mechanism because no one thinks that anyone will donate because we think our government, not just this government, but government after government, it’s just kung sino mas kurap,” he said. — Neil Jayson Servallos

articles.title: Defense dared to answer 3 questions proving VP innocence
articles.summary: As the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte draws to a close, one of the House prosecutors gave an unsolicited advice to their counterparts to help them prove Vice President Sara…

blocks.text: November 25, 2026 | 12:00am
Vice President Sara Duterte on July 30, 2026.
Inday Sara Duterte via Facebook

MANILA, Philippines — As the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte draws to a close, one of the House prosecutors gave an unsolicited advice to their counterparts to help them prove Vice President Sara Duterte’s innocence against charges of unexplained wealth.

According to Akbayan party-list Rep. Chel Diokno, answering three simple questions might help ease the job of the defense in refuting voluminous documents and paper trails about the VP’s questionable assets.

“First, did the Vice President not declare certain assets in her SALN (statement of assets, liabilities and net worth)? Did the VP participate in business while she was VP? And last, did the VP amass wealth that is manifestly disproportionate to her lawful income?” he asked in succession.
Diokno said these are the questions that really matter, because answers to them will determine whether Duterte violated the Constitution or not.
“I think the best way to do it is to stick to what the issues are and to compare those issues with the evidence that’s being presented,” Diokno told “Headstart” on ABS-CBN News yesterday.

“Those are the main questions that must be addressed by the defense and then decided by the court. We are really after the truth and accountability in this proceeding, and we are determined to make sure that that will happen in the days to come,” he emphasized.

The first question concerns whether Duterte accurately disclosed her assets and financial interests in her SALNs, which prosecutors allege contain discrepancies when compared with her financial records.

The second involves Article 7, Section 13 of the Charter, which prohibits her from directly or indirectly participating in business. Prosecutors are examining her business participation and financial interests involving companies linked to her and her husband Manases Carpio.
The third query concerns the prosecution’s forensic accounting findings identifying P817.87 million in alleged unexplained wealth and undeclared assets involving the Duterte couple from 2022 to 2025.

Article II remains the sole Article of Impeachment being pursued before the Senate impeachment court after the House prosecution panel withdrew the other three articles for them to be able to focus more on the financial allegations.
At the same time, Diokno observed that the defense’s withdrawal of their list of witnesses, particularly bank officials, only left crucial financial records against the VP unchallenged.

“So, their decision not to present means that they have not controverted the evidence that comes from the bank accounts and the other evidence upon which Article II is based,” he said. – With Bella Cariaso, Emmanuel Tupas

articles.title: Romualdez: No link to flood control kickbacks
articles.summary: The camp of suspended Leyte Rep. Martin Romualdez maintained there was no evidence linking him to P7.4 billion worth of kickbacks from flood control projects based on information gathered by the…

blocks.text: November 25, 2026 | 12:00am
In this undated photo shows former House Speaker Martin Romualdez
The Philippine STAR / Boy Santos, file photo

MANILA, Philippines — The camp of suspended Leyte Rep. Martin Romualdez maintained there was no evidence linking him to P7.4 billion worth of kickbacks from flood control projects based on information gathered by the Office of the Ombudsman to prepare the probable case of plunder against him.

The prosecution panel from the ombudsman’s office presented as witness Assistant Special Prosecutor II Joshua Ang Tan during the continuation of the hearing on the petition for bail in the plunder case against Romualdez before the Sandiganbayan Third Division yesterday.

Tan was a member of the special panel of prosecutors that filed the plunder charge against Romualdez, fugitive former congressman Zaldy Co, Felicito Guevarra, who recently surrendered to authorities, and Joselyn Serenio, who remains at large.

During cross-examination, Romualdez lawyer Rashel Ann Pomoy asked Tan if in the course of their fact-finding investigation they found any document or interview from witnesses that showed Romualdez “gave Co,” former House appropriations committee chairman, instructions on the national budget, to which he replied, “None.”

Tan gave the same answer when Pomoy pressed him if there was any substandard or “ghost” or non-existent flood control project and any contract named under Romualdez, as well as statements from Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) personnel or contractors that declared Romualdez received kickbacks or commissions.
He confirmed that the ombudsman’s basis for implicating Romualdez was the statement of former DPWH undersecretary Roberto Bernardo that narrated “dealings” between Romualdez and Co.

The defense panel also argued that the two properties allegedly linked to Romualdez were named under two companies – Golden Pheasant Holdings Corp. and Brightnews Corp. – that are both tied to lawyer Jose Raulito Paras as stockholder.

However, Tan maintained that Paras was used by Romualdez, reportedly his fraternity brother, as a front or conduit for the said companies to be able to acquire the subject properties in Makati City, since Paras’ income tax returns hinted his earnings could not match the value of the properties.

During redirect examination by the ombudsman’s Deputy Special Prosecutor Omar Sagadal on why Romualdez was considered the “central figure” in the flood control scandal, Tan said, “You will never be at the front of the scheme yourself, otherwise it will be pointless.”

When asked by Sandiganbayan Associate Justice Ronald Moreno, who presided over the hearing, about the status of any case against Paras, Tan confirmed the ombudsman panel is still in the process of investigating allegations of money laundering against Romualdez and Paras.

Tan told the court that the ombudsman panel gathered “all available interviews and all open-source videos,” which included Co’s video uploaded on social media accusing Romualdez of anomalies, during its fact-finding investigation and called them “leads.”

The leads were later supported by “verified independent evidence,” Tan added, such as the statements from Co’s 18 former security aides who allegedly delivered cash-filled suitcases to the house at 42 McKinley Road, also named under Romualdez, that were used as the basis for the P7.4-billion plunder case.

articles.title: North Korean leader receives Philippine ambassador
articles.summary: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un personally received the credentials of foreign ambassadors, including Philippine Ambassador Jaime FlorCruz, marking the first time in over three decades.

Philippine Ambassador Jaime FlorCruz poses with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un.
STAR / File

MANILA, Philippines — North Korean leader Kim Jong Un personally received the credentials of foreign ambassadors, including Philippine Ambassador Jaime FlorCruz, marking the first time in over three decades.

FlorCruz presented his Letters of Credence to Kim in Pyongyang on Nov. 22, formally assuming his duties as Philippine Ambassador to the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea (DPRK), with residence in Beijing.
The ceremony was the first of such kind officiated by Kim since assuming leadership in 2011. FlorCruz joined nine other recently appointed ambassadors at the event.

In his brief speech during the ceremony, Kim hopes the ambassadors will perform their mission and duty to promote confidence building between their respective countries and the DPRK and to strengthen relations of friendship in conformity with mutual interests.
Based in Beijing as the Philippine ambassador to China, FlorCruz is also the non-resident Philippine ambassador to Mongolia and now DPRK.

articles.title: No agreement on buying 100% US agriculture, energy – Palace
articles.summary: The Philippines has not reached a deal with the United States on sourcing its agriculture and energy supplies, Malacañang clarified yesterday, following business groups’ concerns over…

blocks.text: November 25, 2026 | 12:00am
President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. and US President Donald Trump troop the line during the arrival honors ceremony for Trump’s state visit at the Malacañang Palace on November 18, 2026
The STAR / Noel Pabalate

MANILA, Philippines — The Philippines has not reached a deal with the United States on sourcing its agriculture and energy supplies, Malacañang clarified yesterday, following business groups’ concerns over the announcement that Manila has agreed to buy all its requirements from Washington.

American President Donald Trump claimed last Saturday that President Marcos had agreed to buy 100 percent of the Philippines’ agricultural and energy supplies from the US during their bilateral meeting in Manila.
However, Marcos did not mention an arrangement to source all the Philippines’ agriculture and energy supplies from the US in a media interview in China a day earlier.
The President even highlighted the need to diversify supply sources to minimize risks arising from geopolitical tensions.

Business chambers in the Philippines have urged the Marcos administration to clarify its trade deal with the US, saying the Philippines should not be reliant on a single supplier and should not be compelled to purchase costlier goods.
“There are no terms yet,” Palace press officer Claire Castro said at a media briefing yesterday.

“No details and transactions have been discussed. What was discussed was fast-tracking the possible transactions, speeding up the work from the representative of the Philippines and the representative of the US,” Castro added.
She gave assurance that Marcos would not enter into a deal that would be disadvantageous to the Philippines and its citizens.
Meanwhile, the Department of Foreign Affairs was caught off guard by Trump’s claim, a senator admitted yesterday during plenary debates on the DFA’s proposed P35.2-billion budget for 2027.

Responding to interpellations by Sen. Imee Marcos, DFA budget sponsor Sen. Erwin Tulfo said while DFA officials attended the bilateral meeting between Trump and Marcos during the ASEAN summit, earlier discussions had focused strictly on tariffs.
“Actually, Sen. Imee, everybody was taken aback because this issue was only brought up during the bilateral meeting between the two presidents during the ASEAN,” Tulfo said.
“Prior to this, their discussions were all about tariffs, and there were no issues about importation of agricultural products and any other items,” he added.

Senator Marcos called the lack of prior consultation with foreign policy experts “alarming,” saying Tulfo’s remarks amounted to an admission that the DFA was sidelined despite the geopolitical implications of Trump’s statement.

“I think there’s an admission on the part of the DFA that they were kept in the dark regarding this announcement and that here on after, the matters have been assigned to others. The question that arises of course is who is formulating foreign policy if not the DFA,” Senator Marcos said.
She also flagged what she described as a warning attached to Trump’s remarks.

Tulfo clarified that Malacañang has assigned the trade and agricultural aspects of the matter to the Department of Trade and Industry and the Department of Agriculture, though the DFA continues to monitor developments and awaits further answers from its US counterparts.
The Senate subsequently approved the proposed 2027 budget of the DFA and its attached agencies in plenary. — Neil Jayson Servallos, EJ Macababbad

articles.title: Private schools to hike tuition next year
articles.summary: Officials of the Coordinating Council of Private Educational Associations and the Catholic Educational Association of the Philippines agree that tuition increases are inevitable next school year amid…

blocks.text: November 25, 2026 | 12:00am

At a press conference, COCOPEA chairman Irineo Alvaro Jr. said that like every household, private educational institutions are hit hard by rising inflation, surging electricity and operating costs and frequent calamities.
Pixabay / Tero Vesalainen

MANILA, Philippines — Officials of the Coordinating Council of Private Educational Associations (COCOPEA) and the Catholic Educational Association of the Philippines (CEAP) agree that tuition increases are inevitable next school year amid accelerating inflation.
“These pressures threaten the survival of many schools and make life harder for their students, faculty and staff,” Alvaro said.
Alvaro urged the national government to support policy changes to keep private education sustainable.

“Education agencies should ease strict rules so schools and training institutes can adopt modern, cost-saving and innovative learning modalities without sacrificing quality of education,” Alvaro added.

He said existing tuition fee policies must be reviewed to provide realistic, transparent and timely processes for tuition applications so institutions can sustain fair compensation and support for faculty, invest in modern facilities and continuously improve quality instruction.
“We don’t have other sources, except the support of the government,” Alvaro added.
For his part, Ateneo de Davao University and CEAP president Fr. Karel San Juan said private schools were also affected by the energy crisis amid the war between the United States and Iran.

“If you remember months ago when there was a crisis on energy and fuel because of the war in Iran and the US, all economic forecasts say that it’s going to be a very terrible economy for the Philippines. Our private schools are very sensitive to such economic forecasts because we are really tuition dependent,” San Juan said.
He noted that while the Commission on Higher Education (CHED) asked private schools to suspend tuition fee increases for school year (SY) 2026-2027, some heeded the call of CHED while others did not.

“Why? Because we need to continue running our schools. We need to continue regular across-the-board increases of our faculty and staff. We need to keep pace with the facilities and technological improvements. A simple running of schools will entail increased tuition fees,” San Juan added.
He said the government should allow private schools to decide on tuition fee hikes.

For his part, COCOPEA managing director Joseph Noel Estrada called on CHED and the Department of Education (DepEd) to review the situation. “As my colleagues have said, our tuition guidelines are not only for students but also for faculty and institutions to make them sustainable,” Estrada said.
Education vouchers

Meanwhile, private schools said the enactment of Republic Act 12327 or the Basic Education Voucher Assistance Act is timely as public schools across the country are nearing their breaking point, struggling with packed classrooms, overwhelmed teachers and strained facilities.
Alvaro Jr. said expanding government vouchers to private K-12 schools provides immediate, practical relief by allowing students to move to private basic institutions and decongest public schools.
The law allows students from overcrowded public schools to enroll in private schools using government-funded vouchers.

Signed by the President on Nov. 12, the law will institutionalize a portable, learner-held voucher system, allowing families to choose government-recognized private schools rather than tying subsidies to school-allocated slots under existing programs.

articles.title: Pre-bicam budget meet with economic managers sought
articles.summary: Lawmakers should have a “pre-bicameral” meeting with the country’s economic managers before they overhaul the proposed budget program for 2027, including by ridding it of P54…
articles.byline: Neil Jayson Servallos, Marc Jayson Cayabyab

blocks.text: November 25, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — Lawmakers should have a “pre-bicameral” meeting with the country’s economic managers before they overhaul the proposed budget program for 2027, including by ridding it of P54 billion in allocations for multi-purpose buildings (MPBs) and P85 billion for fragmented cash aid, Sen. Panfilo Lacson said.

In an interview with dzBB radio, Lacson questioned the need to fund 3,950 more MPBs next year, stressing that the government has already spent P770.9 billion on 79,816 MPBs since 2012. This amounts to about 48 MPBs for every city and municipality and 973 for every province.
“Where do we dump all these MPBs? We don’t have real estate, especially in Metro Manila and urban cities. It doesn’t make sense anymore,” Lacson said.

With economic growth slowing to 2.1 percent and inflation hitting 7.8 percent, Lacson said the 2027 budget – crafted under earlier macroeconomic assumptions – no longer matches with current realities and must be realigned toward growth-oriented projects before the bicameral conference committee convenes.

“We should sit down first – economic managers, appropriations committee of the House and the finance committee of the Senate – to have discussions before the bicam because that’s where the real battle is fought,” he said.

He disclosed that his team has so far flagged at least 30 MPBs with double or multiple appropriations, including in Zambales and Pangasinan, as well as a shoreline protection project in Zamboanga that carried a P100-million allocation in the House version without grid coordinates and a separate P95-million item in the Senate version sharing the same coordinates.

In addition to scrapping duplicate projects and the P85 billion in non-4Ps fragmented ayuda – such as MAIFIP, TUPAD and AICS – Lacson reiterated his push for the restoration of the Growth Equity Fund (GEF) for fourth- and fifth-class municipalities, which the Senate trimmed to P8.7 billion from P10.3 billion in the National Expenditure Program and House version. “The situation is difficult. These are extraordinary times,” he said.
Information needed
At Malacañang, Palace press officer Claire Castro urged Lacson to provide information about what he claimed were possible ghost projects in the proposed 2027 national budget.

“Since these are suspected ghost projects, it would be better for Sen. Lacson to inform the DPWH (Department of Public Works and Highways) about the suspected ghost projects or the possible anomalies he saw,” Castro said at a media briefing.
“The President will not allow any anomalous project that would lead to the wastage of public funds and place money on the pockets of the greedy,” she added.
Castro explained that a repeated appropriation is not the same as double appropriation as some projects are implemented in multiple phases.

“We need to authenticate what Sen. Lacson saw because it would be a big help to the government if it is removed. The President would not hesitate to veto it and remove it from the budget if it is really anomalous,” she said. — Alexis Romero, Bella Cariaso

articles.title: School group sees alarming rise in violence, bullying
articles.summary: The Coordinating Council of Private Educational Associations of the Philippines yesterday warned of an alarming rise in school violence, hooliganism and student-on-student bullying across both public…

blocks.text: November 25, 2026 | 12:00am
At a press conference in Taguig, COCOPEA chairman Irineo Alvaro Jr. said addressing violence and bullying in schools requires more than stricter rules and tighter security measures.
edcom2.gov.ph

MANILA, Philippines — The Coordinating Council of Private Educational Associations of the Philippines (COCOPEA) yesterday warned of an alarming rise in school violence, hooliganism and student-on-student bullying across both public and private schools.
“It requires empowering schools, teachers and officials and parents to instill genuine personal discipline and values formation as part of a long-term solution,” Alvaro said.
He urged all educational institutions to reclaim their constitutional role in character formation with courage and clarity.

“Protecting students from abuse and enforcing firm, fair discipline are not opposites – they go hand in hand. While strictly upholding the ban on corporal punishment and all protections against child abuse, schools must stand firmly behind their teachers, consistently enforce clear behavioral standards and partner closely with parents to teach the value of discipline,” Alvaro added.
When homes and schools fail to teach young people accountability, he said, they risk breeding apathy, violence and corruption in society.
“When educational institutions lead with fair and consistent discipline, we shape learners who value their education and become responsible nation-builders,” Alvaro said.
Ateneo de Davao University and Catholic Educational Association of the Philippines (CEAP) president Fr. Karel San Juan said schools should make sure there are sufficient guidance counselors.

“There are many reasons for the increase of bullying and school violence incidents. First, a lot of people say that the general culture of violence may be attributed to the general culture of the youth also. The psychology and emotional well-being of our children are very complex. We need to have very strong, updated and improving formation programs to emphasize values like camaraderie, positive behavior, friendship in our campuses,” San Juan said.
He said schools should make sure that student manuals are aligned with the current laws on bullying, child protection and data protection.

articles.title: Naga administrator named LTO chief; Lacanilao to Marina
articles.summary: The administrator of Naga City has been named new chief of the Land Transportation Office, replacing Markus Lacanilao who has been given a “bigger” assignment as administrator of the…

blocks.text: November 25, 2026 | 12:00am
Noreen Bernadette San Luis and Markus Lacanilao
STAR / File

MANILA, Philippines — The administrator of Naga City has been named new chief of the Land Transportation Office (LTO), replacing Markus Lacanilao who has been given a “bigger” assignment as administrator of the Maritime Industry Authority (MARINA), Malacañang said yesterday.

At a press conference, Palace press officer Claire Castro announced the appointment of former Naga City administrator Noreen Bernadette San Luis as LTO chief and Lacanilao as MARINA administrator, as part of leadership changes in the transport sector aimed at ensuring faster movement of goods as well as safer and comfortable travel for commuters.
“Since former Asec. Markus Lacanilao delivered a good performance and a good message against corruption in LTO, a bigger mission was given to him by the President,” Castro said.

“His appointment as administrator of MARINA is a recognition of his competence because MARINA is at the heart of an industry of 24,000 registered ships and 82 million passenger trips by sea every year,” she added.
“I’m ready, I’m all packed up,” Lacanilao told dzMM after the Palace announcement. Transport group Manibela said its members will continue their strike today to protest the LTO leadership change.

Marcos also appointed Jorjette Aquino as general manager of the Philippine National Railways. Aquino is a former undersecretary of the Presidential Communications Office (PCO), the lead communications arm of the government.

Two key appointees, meanwhile, took their oaths before Marcos yesterday. The President sworn in Douglas Michael Mallillin as chairman of the Commission on Audit (COA) and Maria Angela Ignacio as the new president and chief executive officer of the Maharlika Investment Corp., which manages the country’s sovereign wealth fund.

“The new appointments put two important institutions at the forefront of protecting public resources, promoting accountability and ensuring that government investments contribute to the country’s economic development,” the PCO said in a statement.

Before his appointment as COA commissioner, Mallillin was Director IV under the Office of the Chairperson. A lawyer and certified public accountant, Mallillin was also deputy commissioner at the National Telecommunications Commission, associate prosecutor at the Department of Justice and private legal practitioner at the Edgar M. Avila Law Office. The newly appointed COA chief also taught taxation, business law, accounting and criminal law at St. Louis University and Tarlac State University.
Prior to her appointment to Maharlika, Ignacio was an undersecretary of the finance department.

She was also an undersecretary at the Office of the Special Assistant to the President for Investment and Economic Affairs and managing director of Avisez Asia and of Polestrom. Ignacio also worked as commissioner of the Governance Commission for Government-Owned or Controlled Corporations.

articles.title: BSP chief on peso situation: It’s scary
articles.summary: With its depleting dollar reserves, the country is in a “scary” situation, even as it banks on its $98-billion buffer, Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas Governor Eli Remolona Jr. said at the…

blocks.text: November 25, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — With its depleting dollar reserves, the country is in a “scary” situation, even as it banks on its $98-billion buffer, Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) Governor Eli Remolona Jr. said at the Senate hearing on the national budget yesterday.
Remolona raised the warning after Sen. Imee Marcos pressed him on the decline in the country’s gross international reserves (GIR) to $98 billion from $113 billion.
“Isn’t it scary that our dollar reserves are getting depleted?” Marcos asked Remolona.
“It’s scary,” the BSP chief replied.

Marcos reminded Remolona of his original “safer” target of $104 billion, which he raised during a finance committee budget hearing. He maintained that the $98-billion level is still “a bit safe” because it is equivalent to six months of imports and “three times the country’s short-term debt.”
“So, exports produce the dollars, which are then spent on imports. So that’s the underlying issue,” the BSP official said.
Remolona’s response came amid lawmakers’ mounting concerns over surging inflation, which hit 7.8 percent last month from just 2.4 percent in February.
While Marcos pointed out that the BSP has already raised interest rates four times since March, Remolona said Filipinos would have to wait a year to feel the full impact of the central bank’s move.
“That’s how it is. Its effect on inflation takes about a year. And that’s the best we can do,” he said.

“Unfortunately, we have to contend with the high inflation, as you’ve indicated, and the most effective tool that any country has to slow inflation down is really the policy rate, the interest rate. From experience over 50 years, there’s no other more effective tool than the interest rate,” he added.
He did not rule out further rate hikes. “It’s already high, but so is inflation,” he said.
But for Executive Secretary Ralph Recto, the economy is expected to make a full recovery by the first or second quarter of 2027.
He attributed the current slowdown partly to a deliberate cleanup of the public works budget.

“So we expect a full recovery by the first or second quarter of next year,” Recto told reporters after the Senate’s approval of the Office of the President’s budget during plenary deliberations, when asked about the administration’s economic outlook.

Recto pushed back against claims that the government simply failed to spend on infrastructure, explaining that capital outlays for the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) were slashed from roughly P1 trillion in 2025 to P540 billion in 2026 to weed out flood control projects for review as well as curb irregularities.
“The budget of DPWH from roughly a trillion went down to P540 billion. So because of that, that is the reason for the slowdown among others of the economy with regard to the budget,” he said.
With the DPWH allocation set to rise by roughly P100 billion next year, Recto said the construction industry should see a rebound in 2027.
He added that he has yet to see the entire Senate version of the proposed 2027 budget, which he described as “growth oriented.”
He is set to meet with Budget Secretary Kim Robert de Leon tomorrow to discuss it.

Recto also dismissed US President Donald Trump’s claim that the Philippines would import 100 percent of its energy and agricultural requirements from the United States, stressing that price competitiveness remains the top priority.
“I doubt that very much that 100 percent will happen. I think 100 percent is impossible,” he said.
“What’s important is we are diversifying our sources of energy, sources of food. I think we should welcome that. I think we should also welcome having better trade with our allies,” he added.

Incident took place at the royals’ Sandringham estate country retreat in Norfolk on Monday evening

Two men have been arrested on suspicion of burglary and trespassing at the Prince and…

blocks.text: Two men have been arrested on suspicion of burglary and trespassing at the Prince and Princess of Wales’s country mansion, police have said.
Norfolk police are investigating the suspected break-in at Anmer Hall, a 10-bedroom country retreat given to William and Kate as a gift by Queen Elizabeth II after their wedding.

The force said: “Two men have been arrested on suspicion of burglary following an incident at a property on the Sandringham estate last night. Police were called just before 6pm following a report of suspicious activity at the address.

“Officers attended and specialist resources, including police dogs, drones and the National Police Air Service helicopter, were deployed to assist with searches in the area. Two men were arrested on the estate on suspicion of burglary and trespass. They remain in police custody.”
It is understood no members of the royal family were at home when the alleged burglary took place.

According to the tracking site Flightradar24, a police plane left Nottingham East Midlands airport at 6.25pm on Monday and circled an area close to Sandringham before landing back at the airport almost three hours later.
Anmer Hall, a secluded redbrick Georgian mansion, is on the private Sandringham estate and is a short drive from Sandringham House, one of King Charles’s private residences.
It has its own private swimming pool, a full-size, artificial grass tennis court and vast grounds.
Kensington Palace said it would not comment on security matters.

articles.title: 3 human cases of avian flu confirmed in Washington state, including a death: WHO
articles.summary: The World Health Organization said on Tuesday it had been notified by the United States of three confirmed human cases of bird flu in Washington state, including one death.

image.caption: Three cases of bird flu among humans have been confirmed in Washington state, including one death. Officials say all three were adults who worked on dairy farms in a region where bird flu in cattle was recently detected. (Annie Rice/Reuters)

blocks.text: Health
The World Health Organization said on Tuesday it had been notified by the United States of three confirmed human cases of bird flu in Washington state, including one death.
All worked on dairy farms in county where bird flu was recently detected in cattle
All three cases were adults who worked on dairy farms in the state's Yakima County, where the avian influenza virus was recently detected in cattle, the WHO said.
The UN agency said there was no evidence so far of human-to-human transmission based on information available.

The first patient developed mild symptoms, including eye irritation and a runny nose, and was not hospitalized. The second, who had underlying medical conditions, developed severe respiratory illness and died on Nov. 1. The third developed conjunctivitis and recovered without hospitalization.
Genetic sequencing confirmed all three infections were caused by the H5N1 virus, with strains closely matching those detected in dairy cattle in Washington.
H5N1 bird flu is a subtype of influenza A virus that primarily infects wild and domestic birds, and occasionally spreads to mammals, including humans.
A researcher uses a pipette to transfer a sample into a microtube as researchers work to monitor avian influenza, at the Institut Pasteur in Paris, on Nov. 24. (Gonzalo Fuentes/Reuters)

While the current public health risk is low, the U.S. Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) is watching the situation carefully and working with states to monitor people with animal exposures.
The CDC has reported 75 human H5 infections since February 2024, including the three cases in Washington.
Canada has never recorded a case of avian flu in the dairy industry, but officials in British Columbia are monitoring the situation directly south of them.
Dr. Theresa Burns, B.C.'s chief veterinarian, said earlier this week that all cattle imported from the U.S. are tested and tracked, and that it’s mandatory to report infected livestock.

items: U.S. records 1st human bird flu death since last year
B.C. watching closely after Washington state death linked to avian flu in dairy industry
This Sask. woman took some birds to a poultry show. Now avian flu is taking her whole flock

blocks.text: "I'm confident in the measures that we're taking together with the [B.C.] Dairy Association,” she said.

No human cases of avian flu have been reported in Canada since a B.C. teenager contracted the virus in 2024 and suffered serious illness before recovering. But avian flu among poultry flocks has seen an increase this month in the wake of a national poultry show. As of last Thursday, the Canadian Food Inspection Agency had confirmed 11 cases of the avian flu connected to the Canadian National Poultry Show held on Nov. 7 in Moose Jaw.

articles.title: Trump made up to $15m on Nvidia stock after Huang’s return
articles.summary: US president says he ‘convinced’ chipmaker’s board to reinstate CEO, as Nvidia shares fall after previous day’s rally

blocks.text: Donald Trump made up to $15m (£11.5m) on his holdings of Nvidia stock after the US chipmaker’s share price soared on the surprise return of Jensen Huang as chief executive.

Huang, who co-founded the company in 1993, was ousted by the board after allegations that he had three affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy and two with employees. But the Nvidia board reinstated him after an intervention from the US president.
“I spoke to them, let me put it that way,” Trump told CNBC on Monday. “And I convinced them … I made the deal.”

The US president’s financial disclosures to the Office of Government Ethics indicate he might have owned as many as 370,000 shares in Nvidia as of 30 September, the latest available data, in news first reported by the Financial Times.

Nvidia’s shares rocketed by 31.5% on Monday, adding about $950bn to the company’s value. Huang returned to the company’s HQ in Santa Clara, California, receiving a hero’s welcome, with crowds of employees chanting “Jensen, Jensen, Jensen!”

Trump has bought shares of Nvidia stock worth between $23m and $86m, according to a BBC review of his government financial disclosures for the past two years. He has also sold some of his stake in the company since returning to the presidency, and gained between $3.5m and $10.2m, according to his government disclosures.
Huang’s surprising, and controversial, return to run Nvidia – which is at the heart of the global AI boom – prompted a strong rally in Asia-Pacific stock markets on Tuesday.

Stocks soared in Taiwan, South Korea, Japan and Australia, as the AI trade lurched back into life after a tumultuous few months. Taiwan’s TW50 index leapt by 9.5%, while South Korea’s Kospi index jumped by 6.5%, led by the chipmakers SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics. Japan’s Nikkei gained almost 4%. Stock markets across Europe were broadly flat.

In the US, stock markets opened down, with the S&P 500 off 0.4% and the tech heavy Nasdaq down 1.8%. Nvidia’s shares fell 6% in early trading. Anthropic, the AI company which sold shares in its record-breaking flotation last week, saw its stock drop by 8.3% at the start of trading, to $80.34, below the $83 IPO price.
after newsletter promotion

That followed a rise on Wall Street on Monday. AI shares have been on a rollercoaster in recent months, amid worries over high debt levels in the sector to fund the AI infrastructure buildout, as well as the prospect of tougher regulation in the US after the Democrats’ victory in the midterm elections.

Ruben Gallego, a Democrat senator from Arizona, posted on X: “We need to investigate what stock positions took place before the announcement. This White House is the most corrupt in history.” He later posted: “Trump may have started the popping of the AI bubble.”

Roger Lee, the head of equity strategy at the investment bank Cavendish, said: “Given Nvidia’s pivotal role in the AI capex rollout, the implications of Huang’s reinstatement could be profound. Borrowing from the [global financial crisis], are some technology CEOs now so systemically important to the future of AI and US leadership in the latest technology revolution that they cannot be fired?

“Questions around the scale of financing required and future monetisation remain, and the dependence on Huang for the future success of AI may paradoxically heighten those concerns especially given Anthropic fell despite yesterday’s broad market rally.”
Economists said Huang’s return meant the US Federal Reserve was more likely to raise interest rates, with the prospect of the AI bubble bursting imminently diminishing.
Jim Reid of Deutsche Bank said: “With fears of an AI slowdown receding, it also led markets to price back in a more hawkish path for the Federal Reserve over the months ahead.
“So for the next meeting in December, markets are once again fully pricing in a 25 basis point hike.”

articles.title: Pope Francis diaries recount spiritual crisis, him seeing the 'Devil'
articles.summary: Extracts of the late Pope Francis' diaries have been published, the first release of its kind since the 1960s. They discuss his struggles with his role in the Vatican and visions of the devil and the…

image.caption: The Vatican has released 'The personal diary of Pope Francis' on the mass market, with accompanying commentary from a friend of the late pope, Cardinal Victor Manuel FernandezImage: Monica Giuliani/CatholicPressPhoto/IPA/ABACA/picture alliance

blocks.text: The late Pope Francis suffered a spiritual crisis during his papacy when he struggled with how to lead the Catholic Church and believed he saw and heard the devil on several occasions, according to an annotated collection of his private diaries published on Tuesday.
Francis was pope for 12 years until his death last April.

Cardinal Victor Fernandez, a compatriot and close collaborator of Francis', collated the diary entries and provides accompanying commentary, in the first set of papal diaries to be published posthumously since those of John XXIII, who died in 1963.

blocks.caption: The 160-page sample of Francis' diaries is the first release of its kind in more than 50 yearsImage: Gregorio Borgia/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: What does the book say about Francis' difficulties as pope?
The diary entries speak of the Argentine-born pontiff not wanting to be someone "who uses others like puppets," according to the accompanying commentary.
"It was all mixed with governance issues, pressure regarding decisions to make, and aridity and desolation," a December 2022 entry from Francis said.

Although the book does not make clear exactly who Francis worried he was using like puppets or the nature of the internal pressures, Francis encountered stern resistance from more conservative forces within the Church as he urged the staid institution to modernize.

Cardinal Fernandez wrote that Francis "ultimately recognized it was the worst trial that had toremented him ... and that he felt that he was in a continual battle not to fall into this demonic seduction."

blocks.caption: Various world leaders attended Francis' funeral last April [FILE: April 2025]Image: IPA/ABACAPRESS/IMAGO

blocks.text: What does the book say about Francis' religious visions and dreams?

The 160-page selection of excerpts — starting in 1992 when he was still known as Jorge Mario Bergoglio and running until a few months before his death — are arranged by theme and pay closer attention to Francis' internal spiritual experiences than Vatican politics.

But one of the three occasions listed where the late pope believed he had seen the Devil was during a meeting with Vatican officials in January 2021 early in what he termed a spiritual crisis. In that instance he even believed to have heard the figure speak.
"I can't forget the powerful raspiness of his voice," Francis wrote in an entry. "The Lord granted me an opportunity to leave that meeting, and thus he freed me."
Other entries detail how Francis believed that God spoke to him in his dreams, and one from 2018 stated: "Last night I saw the entrance to Hell. I peeked in to look a little, and it terrified me."
Pope Francis' life and legacy
What else features in the diary excerpts?

The papers show Francis to be self-critical at times, chastizing himself for "feelings of disdain, envy, pride" or for ignoring a drunken man who approached him "because I wanted to have a serene walk."
At one point in a 2022 entry he refers to himself as the "proud, self-sufficient, cynical, self-deceptive Jorge."
They also show how in later years he felt anxious to make the most of his remaining years, and regretful about some of his deicsions earlier in his life.
"I want to do good during the little time I have left, desiring to be good," he wrote in 1996 on turning 60. "How much time I've used badly! How much badly done!"

The accounts also list his regret after a visit to Chile in 2018 when he faced stern criticism for initially dismissing allegations of sexual abuse and cover-up against a bishop there before later apologizing.
"It was hard for me to admit what happened in Chile; I didn't think it was so serious," a "devastated" pontiff wrote three years later.

Fernandez also recounts comments from Francis on some senior officials in the Vatican including his successor, US Cardinal Robert Prevost, now Pope Leo XIV. According to Fernandez, Francis called him "a great pastor, a generous missionary, and an irreproachable man."

blocks.caption: The diaries' collator says Francis was highly complimentary of the man who succeeded him, Robert Francis Prevost or Pope Leo XIV [FILE: September 2023]Image: Romano Siciliani/Avalon/Photoshot/picture alliance
